## Smoking Pathophysiology

Smoking → keratinization of mucosa → quitting → thinning → ulceration → advise nicotine replacement

Heavy smoking has an adverse effect upon the healing (carbon monoxide, tissue hypoxia, hydrogen cyanide). Greater the consumption & duration, greater the significance of tobacco as co-factor for MRONI.

# Stress

* Stress and psychosomatic disorder may likely impact periodontal health via change in individuals' behaviour and through complex interactions among the nervous, endocrine & immune systems.

* Individuals with stress have poorer oral hygiene, they may start clenching/grinding their teeth & may smoke more frequently.

* Chronic stress & inadequate coping can lead to physiologic changes such as ↓ salivary flow and suppressed immunity.

* Onset of ulcers may be attributed to elevated levels of salivary cortisols or reactive oxygen species. Immunity also increase immune regulatory activity in inflammation by increasing the quantity & activity of leukocytes.
